My farm is only 4.1 mu, so I follow the wheat-maize double cropping that everyone here in Quzhou does. With six people in the household and some working off-farm, this land mostly feeds the family and brings a little cash. I have been doing this 30 years, so I do not experiment much — I stick with what works and adjust a little each year.

For the winter wheat this autumn, I will plant Jimai 22 — most of my neighbors use it and it handles our dry spring well. On 4.1 mu I will use about 15 kg of seed per mu because I broadcast-drill and want a good stand. Base fertilizer I put down with rotary tillage: one bag of 15-15-15 compound per mu (that gives me about 7.5 kg each of N, P, K), plus I topdress urea at jointing in spring, about 15 kg urea per mu (another 7 kg N). So total N around 14-15 kg/mu. I know the agronomists say we overuse nitrogen in this county, but I would rather spend the extra 20 yuan on urea than risk a thin crop. Irrigation: I pump from the well three times — once before sowing if dry, then green-up and jointing in spring. If May is dry I add a fourth at grain filling. Herbicide once in late autumn for broadleaf weeds, then one spray in April for aphids and rust. I expect 500 kg/mu — that is what I got last year.

For summer maize after wheat harvest in June, I use Zhengdan 958, direct seeded no-till into the wheat stubble to save time and moisture. One bag of compound fertilizer at sowing (7-8 kg N, 7 P, 7 K per mu), then topdress urea 20 kg/mu at the big trumpet stage — that brings total N to about 16 kg/mu. Maize here needs less irrigation than wheat because of summer rain; usually just one watering at tasseling if July is dry. Two pesticide sprays — one for armyworm/corn borer, one for aphids. I expect around 550 kg/mu.
